# NOT the 2022 tune of that seed: legacy/examples/out_1655110192_5500_200.ogg was made with the Apple generator,
# which the new program does not have. This list is the v10 rules run with the Linux (glibc) generator;
# no recording of it exists.
# Produced by the code in legacy/ (harmonics.c, harmonics-util.c, harmonics-dingdong.c) with v10_trace.patch applied:
#     ./harmonics_trace 1655110192 200 3440     (srand(1655110192), glibc rand(), totalSongTime = 200, binsPerSlot = 3440)
#     python3 trace_to_tones.py events.txt 200
# The traced program's out.wav is byte for byte the out.wav of the unpatched source given the same seed, cycles and binsPerSlot.
# Covers cycles 0..169 (ticks 0..1869): everything before the end phase. 174 tones; the last one starts at tick 1866.
# The first tone (56.5 Hz) lies outside 100..3000 Hz, which the v10 rules allow for the first tone only.
# There is always a counted tone, so every tone has a level draw.
# A new composer given the same rules, generator, seed and cycles must reproduce this list exactly.
#
# tick     slot boundary index; cycle = tick / 11, slot = tick % 11
# parent   tick at which the tone it derives from was created (the tone then occupying the previous slot)
# ratio    exact frequency ratio to the parent tone
# freq_hz  resulting frequency (double, 17 significant digits)
# pan      0 = left .. 1 = right
# reps     repetition count N: struck N+1 times, once per cycle, at gain N/N, (N-1)/N, .. 0/N
# level    the tone's own volume, above 0 and at most 1 (the first tone: 0.7), written with the fewest digits
#          that read back as the same double. A tone is a counted tone if its level is above 0.69.
# jitter   raw 0..99 draw; the 2011 sound uses it for the vibrato period, 18000 * (1 + 0.001 * jitter)
#          samples at 44.1 kHz ('-' = no draw, 18000)
#
